title: Macaroni Cheese
subtitle: British béchamel-and-cheddar pasta bake
excerpt: Macaroni cooked in a proper mature cheddar béchamel, then baked with a breadcrumb top until golden and bubbling. The British version uses sharp cheddar and a well-seasoned white sauce.

recipe.sourceNotes: Macaroni cheese appears in British cookery writing from the eighteenth century. Mrs Beeton's 1861 version uses a béchamel base, cheddar, and a breadcrumb crust baked until golden, a template that has changed very little. The American version developed its own identity with processed cheese; the British household version stayed with cheddar and white sauce.

recipeTools.notes: For the béchamel and cooking the pasta.
A 30 x 20 cm dish for baking.

content.text: Macaroni cheese is a béchamel that has absorbed a lot of cheddar, poured over just-cooked macaroni and finished in the oven until the top browns. The béchamel is the skill, too thin and the dish is watery, too thick and it sets solid. The right consistency is thick enough to coat a spoon but still pourable. Mature cheddar is essential; mild cheddar makes a flat-tasting sauce.
Cook the macaroni in a large pot of salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet time, it will finish cooking in the oven. Drain and set aside.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir constantly for 2 minutes to form a smooth paste. Remove from the heat.

Add the milk a little at a time, whisking after each addition to keep the sauce smooth. Return to medium heat and stir constantly until the sauce thickens and bubbles, about 8 to 10 minutes. It should coat the back of a spoon thickly.
Remove from the heat. Stir in three-quarters of the cheddar, the mustard, salt, and pepper. Taste, the sauce should be savoury and sharp. Add the drained macaroni and stir to combine.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Pour the mixture into a buttered baking dish. Scatter the remaining cheddar over the surface, then the breadcrumbs. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden and the sauce is bubbling at the edges. Leave to settle for 5 minutes before serving.
